outcome: No result establishing, refuting, or narrowing any new case of Nagata's conjecture on curves was found in the window 26 January 2024 to 22 September 2026; the conjecture remains open for every non-perfect-square r ≥ 10, exactly as it stood in January 2024.
summary: Nagata's conjecture on curves (1959) predicts that a plane curve of degree d passing through r ≥ 10 very general points of P² with multiplicity at least m at each point must satisfy d > m√r; Nagata himself proved it when r is a perfect square, and every non-square case r ≥ 10 has been open for over 60 years. I ran searches for direct progress ('Nagata's conjecture proof/disproof 2024 2025 2026'), for the modern Seshadri-constant formulation, for the Nagata–Biran generalization, for bound improvements, and specifically for any AI-mathematics connection. The only post-2024 item that surfaced is Galindo–Monserrat–Moreno-Ávila–Moyano-Fernández, 'On the valuative Nagata conjecture,' published in Research in the Mathematical Sciences 12, no. 18 (2025) — but this is the journal publication of arXiv:2208.11041, whose only version was submitted 23 August 2022, well before the frozen revision. Per the dating rule (date by first written argument, not journal date), this event predates the window entirely and in any case is a different, weaker 'valuative' variant (concerning minimality of plane divisorial valuations w.r.t. an ample divisor, only implying the classical conjecture, not equivalent to or settling it) that gives equivalent characterizations of minimality rather than proving the valuative conjecture itself — so even setting the date aside it would not count as a case of this problem under §3.1. I also confirmed that a separate, distinctly named 'Nagata's conjecture' concerning wild automorphisms of polynomial rings (proved by Umirbaev and Shestakov in 2004, well before the window) and the triage-flagged September 2026 positive-characteristic automorphism variant are unrelated problems sharing only the name Nagata, not cases of this curves conjecture. No AI-mathematics coverage (OpenAI, Anthropic/Claude, or other lab announcements about conjecture-solving) mentions Nagata's conjecture on curves; the AI breakthroughs I found in that space (Jacobian conjecture counterexample, cycle double cover conjecture, Erdős conjectures) are unrelated problems. The current live Wikipedia article's lead and body are unchanged in substance from the frozen revision and cite nothing later than 2004. I am satisfied this is a genuine 'nothing happened' result.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2025 journal publication of the valuative Nagata conjecture paper should be recorded as an 'event' under status progress, since it is the first fully peer-reviewed, expert-digested appearance of that variant's equivalent characterizations. But (a) the substantive mathematical content was already public via the 2022 arXiv preprint, before the window, and (b) the valuative Nagata conjecture is a distinct (stronger, implying) conjecture about divisorial valuations, not a case of the classical curves conjecture as restricted by prescribed multiplicities at finitely many very general points — it is a related problem under §3.1, not a case, since it changes the object (a valuation rather than a finite point set) rather than merely restricting it. Either way it would not move this record off 'open'.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint or announcement, dated after 26 January 2024, that either (a) proves or disproves Nagata's conjecture for some new non-square r ≥ 10, or (b) proves the general case, or (c) exhibits an AI system's involvement in either. None of these were found.
